spec_match.rationale: Uses the real chunked startRendering loop for the exact purpose the explainer motivates — bounded memory and genuine progress during faster-than-real-time mixdown — and measures the actual peak float allocation instead of asserting it.

interactive.rationale: One button runs the whole pipeline: real multi-oscillator render, per-chunk progress bar updates, incremental waveform, live stats tiles, and a downloadable WAV built from accumulated Int16 parts.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises progress + incremental WAV + labelled legacy fallback; all three are delivered and the mode tile states which path ran.

edge_cases.rationale: The one-shot fallback is first-class: clearly labelled, still produces the WAV, and the status text explains exactly what degrades (two-state progress, full-buffer memory); exceptions are shown verbatim and object URLs are revoked between runs.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5109900936085504 and the explainer's memory motivation; crumbs reach the full reference list.

conformance.rationale: The suite's chunk-return and trim assertions are the contracts this exporter relies on; the shared panel runs them on-page.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): run clicked; legacy path correctly detected (1 call, peak 132,300 frames), progress reached 100, stats tiles filled, waveform painted, 258 KB WAV download link produced with byte count matching 44 + frames×2; zero console errors, zero failed requests, 0px overflow, desktop screenshot read. Partial: the chunked path (peak 8192 frames, ~17 progress steps) needs a 158+ build.

telemetry_health.rationale: oac-exporter-wav-complete asserts rendered frames and blob size agree; failures route to a verbatim status instead of silent console errors.

design_system.rationale: Stats tiles and download link use design-system pairs at AA; the download link is a bordered ivory surface with text-black.

accessibility.rationale: Native labelled progress element driven by real completion, canvas as role=img with description, stats duplicated as text tiles, status is aria-live=polite, download is a real link with a filename.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: responsive-check matrix run for the feature id: mobile 360×740 DPR3 and desktop 1280×800, no horizontal overflow, console/network clean, both screenshots read; tiles reflow via auto-fit minmax.

openQuestions.title: Measure the chunked memory profile on a Chrome 158+ build
openQuestions.detail: On a 158+ build, verify the mode tile reads chunked, the peak tile reports 8192 frames (32 KB), progress advances in ~17 steps, and the produced WAV is byte-identical in size to the legacy path's output.

guidanceConsulted.query: long running task progress bar accessible
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use the native progress element with a programmatic label and drive it from real completion state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The exporter's progress is a labelled native <progress> updated only when a real chunk resolves — on legacy builds it honestly jumps 0→100 and the status says why.

guidanceConsulted.query: download link generated file accessible name
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Generated artifacts should be real links with descriptive names and sizes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The WAV is an anchor with filename and size in its text; object URLs from prior runs are revoked.

summary: Product mixdown exporter: chunked render driving real progress, incremental PCM accumulation and a WAV download, with a labelled one-shot fallback. Driven on headless Chromium 141 (repo CDP harness; no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment): legacy path verified end-to-end including the produced file, clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
